overall_structure.value: Single ferrite phase (BCC, disordered Fe-Al) stabilized by Al addition, containing nano-sized Fe3Al ordered phase (DO3 structure). Mössbauer spectroscopy reveals Al atoms distributed both in solid solution and as ordered phase, splitting the spectral response into multiple hyperfine-field components; SAXS shows a weak nano-sized ordered-phase scattering peak between q = 0.3 and 3 nm^-1.

source.reason: Overall microstructure of the Fe-9Al powder sample: single ferrite phase with nano-sized Fe3Al (DO3) ordered phase, as characterized by Mössbauer spectroscopy and SAXS on powder samples annealed at 600 °C for 60 min.
Al addition up to ~10 wt% stabilizes the BCC ferrite phase; the XRD/analysis of the Fe-Al alloys confirms formation of the ferrite phase.
Formation of nano-sized Fe3Al ordered phase with DO3 structure established by Mössbauer, SAXS and TEM; the volume fraction of the SAXS-observed ordered phase increases with Al content (Fig. 4).

distribution.value: Nano-sized ordered phase distributed in the ferrite matrix; the ordered-phase diameter increased from 2.5 ± 0.15 nm to 3.75 ± 0.2 nm with increasing Al content, so 9 wt% Al (Fe-9Al) has the largest ordered-phase size of the series.

source.reason: SAXS vs Mössbauer comparison of the ordered phase boundary nature and the Al-content dependence of ordered phase size/volume fraction.
The ordered Fe3Al phase is embedded in the ferrite matrix; SAXS provides collective information about the ordered phase having a sharper boundary while Mössbauer traces diffused boundaries.

coherence.value: SAXS indicates the ordered phase has a sharper boundary, whereas Mössbauer spectroscopy traces all local environments including those with diffused boundaries.

phase_evolution.value: With increasing Al content the volume fraction and size of the Fe3Al ordered phase increase, owing to the increasing driving force for ordered-phase formation with increasing Al addition (wt%). For Fe-9Al (9 wt% Al) this gives the largest ordered-phase size and volume fraction of the studied compositions.

interface_notes.value: The ordered phase interface interpretation is drawn from combining SAXS (sharp boundaries) and Mössbauer spectroscopy (all local environments, including diffused boundaries); no direct TEM interface characterization was performed on the 600 °C/60 min powder sample (TEM was performed on Fe-6.8Al).

source.reason: Mössbauer spectroscopy was carried out on the filed/annealed powder samples including Fe-9Al; Table 1 gives the Fe-9Al hyperfine-field components, and the text describes the ~23 T and 30.6 T components.

instrument_or_setup.value: Conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source; velocity of the drive calibrated by a pure iron (α-Fe) foil.

measurement_conditions.value: Room temperature, transmission geometry, on filed powder annealed at 600 °C for 60 min.

purpose.value: Examine the formation of ordered phases and the distribution of local atomic configurations (Al in solid solution vs ordered phase) in the Fe-Al low-density steels, including Fe-9Al.

key_findings.value: Fe-9Al shows the shallowest and most broadened sextet of the series (Transmission 96-100 %); the P(B_hf) distribution is deconvoluted into multiple components. Table 1 lists 10 components for Fe-9Al with B_hf (±0.5 T) / Area (±1%) / V_f (±1%) / assignment: 32.68 T / 8.55 % / 7.7 % / (8Fe)nn+(5Fe+1Al)nnn; 30.34 T / 45.45 % / 44 % / (7Fe+1Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn or (8Fe)nn+(6Al)nnn; 27.54 T / 31.9 % / 33 % / (6Fe+2Al)nn+(4Fe+2Al)nnn; 25.21 T / 10.4 % / 11.4 % / (5Fe+3Al)nn+(5Fe+1Al)nnn; 23.31 T / 3.7 % / 4.2 % / (4Fe+4Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn; 32.62 T / 7.9 % / 7.2 % / (8Fe)nn+(5Fe+1Al)nnn; 30.31 T / 44.1 % / 42.3 % / (7Fe+1Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn or (8Fe)nn+(6Al)nnn; 27.79 T / 26.8 % / 27.8 % / (6Fe+2Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn; 25.48 T / 17.5 % / 18.9 % / (5Fe+3Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn; 22.97 T / 3.1 % / 3.6 % / (4Fe+4Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn. A low-intensity peak at ~23 T (present for Al content 6, 6.8, 9 wt%) is a possible indicator of Fe3Al (B2) phase with a low volume fraction. A component at B_hf = 30.6 T observed in all studied Fe-Al steels may be associated with (7Fe+1Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn (or with the Fe3Al phase corresponding to (8Fe)nn+(6Al)nnn).

source.reason: SAXS measurements on the powder samples (including Fe-9Al) provide the ordered-phase diameter and volume fraction; the 9 wt% Al point gives the upper-end diameter 3.75 ± 0.2 nm.

instrument_or_setup.value: Laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France); camera lengths 550 and 2400 mm; 2D profiles azimuthally integrated to 1D using FIT2D software; intensity converted to absolute scale using glassy carbon as secondary standard; Silver-Behenate powder used to calibrate the scattering angle.

measurement_conditions.value: Transmission geometry; measurement time 4-6 h; q-range 0.0254 to 10 nm^-1; powder sandwiched between Scotch Magic tape.

purpose.value: Quantify the size, volume fraction and number density of the nano-sized ordered DO3 phase in the Fe-Al low-density steels.

key_findings.value: Nano-sized ordered phase scattering appears as a weak peak between q = 0.3-3 nm^-1, with the intensity increasing (and Guinier region shifting to low q) with Al content; at low q (<0.3 nm^-1) intensity decays as q^-4 (Porod scattering) from larger heterogeneities (grains/grain boundaries). The Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter for Fe-9Al (9 wt% Al) is 3.75 ± 0.2 nm (largest of the series) with the corresponding volume fraction increasing to just below the 2.0 % level (Fig. 4).

source.reason: The Mössbauer spectrum of each Fe-Al composition (including Fe-9Al) was fitted with the NORMOS program using Eq. (1), giving the P(B_hf) distribution.

simulation_method.value: Fitting of the experimentally measured Mössbauer spectrum of the Fe-9Al sample by a superimposition of the distribution of sextets (up to 40 sextets) corresponding to different values of the hyperfine magnetic field B_hf, to obtain the probability distribution P(B_hf).

validation_against_experiment.value: The fitted P(B_hf) distributions reproduce the experimentally measured Mössbauer spectra of the Fe-9Al sample (Fig. 1i,j).

model_name.value: Hyperfine field vs local atomic configuration (Eq. 1)

equation_role.value: Relates the observed B_hf to the local atomic configuration of first and second nearest non-magnetic (Al) neighbours: B = B0 - n1*ΔB1 - n2*ΔB2.

model_note.value: n1 and n2 are the numbers of Al atoms in the first and second nearest neighbours; ΔB1 and ΔB2 values were taken from Ref. [26].

source.reason: SAXS intensity profiles of the Fe-Al alloys (including Fe-9Al) were fitted with the local mono-disperse model (Eqs. 2-5) to obtain the ordered-phase size and volume fraction.

simulation_method.value: Nonlinear curve fitting of the SAXS intensity profiles I(q) with a local mono-disperse model, assuming a log-normal number-density distribution of spherical ordered phase particles, to estimate size, volume fraction and number density of the ordered DO3 phase.

software_used.value: FIT2D (azimuthal integration of 2D-SAXS profiles); mono-disperse model fit per Eqs. (2)-(5)

validation_against_experiment.value: The fitted curves agree well with the experimental SAXS intensities (Fig. 3), and the resulting ordered-phase sizes are consistent between the SAXS-observed values and the TEM-measured values for the ordered phase.

equation_role.value: Describes the scattering intensity I(q) = Δρ^2 * dN * ∫ N(r)[V(r)F(q,r)]^2 dr, with a log-normal size distribution N(r) and spherical form factor F(q,r), to extract the size, volume fraction and number density of the ordered phase.

name.value: Δρ (scattering length difference between Fe3Al DO3 ordered phase and disordered Fe-Al matrix)

model_note.value: Form factor F(q,r) is that of a sphere; at high q, F^2(q,r) shows q^-4 dependence (Porod scattering).

unmapped_findings: Fe-9Al (9 wt% Al) is the highest-Al composition among the studied binary Fe-Al low-density steels (5, 6, 6.8 and 9 wt% Al); across the series the SAXS-measured Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter increased from 2.5 ± 0.15 nm (5 wt% Al) to 3.75 ± 0.2 nm (9 wt% Al), i.e. Fe-9Al has the largest ordered-phase diameter and volume fraction.

For the Fe-9Al powder sample the SAXS-observed ordered-phase volume fractions are lower than the DO3-phase volume fractions observed by Mössbauer spectroscopy, because SAXS provides collective information about the ordered phase having a sharper boundary whereas Mössbauer spectroscopy traces all local environments, including those having diffused boundaries.

The Mössbauer P(B_hf) distribution of Fe-9Al (Fig. 1i,j) is the shallowest and most broadened of the series (sextet spanning ~96-100 % transmission), deconvoluted into several green Gaussian components spanning roughly 25-34 T.

Reference hyperfine fields for Fe-Al ordered phases: DO3 (Fe3Al) ≈ 30 T and B2 (FeAl) ≈ 21 T (reported for Al > 24 wt%); Fe3Al also has an associated hyperfine-field component ((4Fe+4Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn) at ~21 T, and a ~23 T low-intensity peak (seen for Al content 6, 6.8 and 9 wt%, i.e. including Fe-9Al) is a possible indicator of the Fe3Al phase with a low volume fraction.

Alloy composition (Fe with 9 wt% Al) was produced by vacuum arc melting of interstitial free (IF) steel and pure Al charges re-melted 7-8 times; the exact WDS/EPMA composition is reported in Ref. [15] and the paper states the composition throughout the text corresponds to aluminium content in wt%.
